title: Second objection: no created gift first wins God's favour
source_text: IX. Deinde iis non probatur quod quidquam in nobis creatum & inhaerens dicatur gratia Deo gratum atque acceptum faciens, ut videre est apud Polanum Aretium & Petrum Martyrem locis supra citatis. Non quod negent Dei dona, quae Scholae Rom. Doctores per gratiam gratum facientem designant, esse aliquid Deo placens, quo Deus delectetur, & quod ipsi gratum sit: Sed quod istis donis non primum Dei favor hominibus conciliatur; cum ipsa sint effecta favoris & amoris divini, & procedant a Deo nobis favente, nosque diligente, etiam antequam illa acceperimus: juxta illud Joannis, Non quod dilexerimus Deum, sed quia prior ipse dilexit nos.
pass_a_gloss: IX. Next it is not approved by them that anything created and inhering in us be called grace making pleasing and accepted to God, as is to be seen in Polanus Aretius and Peter Martyr in the places cited above. Not that they deny that the gifts of God, which the Doctors of the Rom. School designate by grace making pleasing, are something pleasing to God, in which God delights, and which is pleasing to him: But that by these gifts the favour of God is not first won for men; since they themselves are effects of divine favour and love, and proceed from God favouring us, and loving us, even before we received them: according to that of John, Not that we loved God, but because he first loved us.
pass_b_english: Thesis IX. Second, they do not accept that anything created and inhering in us should be called grace that makes us pleasing and acceptable to God, as can be seen in Polanus, Aretius and Peter Martyr at the places cited above.

They do not deny that the gifts which the doctors of the Roman school mean by grace that makes pleasing are something that pleases God, something he delights in and finds acceptable. Their point is that these gifts are not what first wins God's favour for people. The gifts are themselves effects of God's favour and love, and they come from God already favouring and loving us even before we received them. As John says: not that we loved God, but because he first loved us.

choices.term: gratia gratis data ... gratia gratum faciens
choices.english: grace freely given ... grace that makes pleasing
choices.why: The scholastic pair (Aquinas, Summa theologiae I-II q. 111 a. 1): gifts given for the good of others versus the grace that makes its bearer pleasing to God. Kept literal because the Reformed objections turn on the very words.
